To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified 21 D meson candidates produced in association with the π − in the 340 GeV/c beam.

we have found 21 charmed particle candidates in a sample of 340 GeV pions interacting in a C 3 F bubble chamber, and that the cross section for associated production of charmed particles in nucleon-nucleon interactions is about 30 μb per nucle on.
the cross section for associated production of charmed mesons by 340 Gev/c pion beam is (28± 11) micro-b per nucleon assuming an A -dependence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new methods in experimental high energy physics, in particular in the field of heavy ion collisions.

the development and use of the heavy liquid bubble chambers (HLBC) for the study of the properties of the charmed particles produced in the interactions of π −, K −, and p at 340 GeV/ c with a nuclear target.
the study of the structure of the proton in its ground state and in excited states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the charmed particles are indeed produced and their lifetimes are of the same order of magnitude as predicted by the current theoretical models.

, in the present stage of our knowledge, the data are compatible with the hypothesis of a new quark, c, with mass 1.5 ± 0.2 GeV c −2 and charge (2/3)e, and that the charmed mesons D 0,D ±, and D 0 are produced with a cross section of about 30μb per nucleon.
the data are consistent with the production of charmed particles, but that the statistical accuracy is not yet sufficient to exclude other interpretations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found 21 D -mesons, 4 of which decayed into K − π + π +.
we have found the first evidence for the D 0 and D ±, and have measured the lifetimes of the charmed mesons.
the D 0 and D 0 have similar lifetimes, and the D ± has a lifetime longer than the D 0 by about a factor of 2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mean lifetime of D 0 mesons is significantly shorter than that of the D ± mesons.
the BIBC is an ideal tool to measure the properties of short lived particles.
it is possible to use an existing bubble chamber as a particle detector for the study of rare processes.
